primary_evidence.title: SQLite Write-Ahead Logging
primary_evidence.version: Live official page last updated 2026-08-25 19:42:39Z; applied to stipulated SQLite 3.51.3
primary_evidence.retrieval_operation: Independent direct web open; complete relevant surrounding passages read
locators: 9 Sometimes Queries Return SQLITE_BUSY In WAL Mode
primary_evidence.evidence_summary: Single writer; readers constrain checkpoint progress/reset; same-host shared memory; read-only support since 3.22.0 has three conditions; WAL is persistent state; physical reuse differs from truncation; performance is workload-dependent; WAL-reset fix is in 3.51.3.
primary_evidence.applicability: Ordinary shared-memory-capable VFS, same-host processes, local disk. Single-process exclusive-lock/custom-VFS exceptions change the assigned design.

primary_evidence.title: SQLite checkpoint C interface
primary_evidence.version: Live unversioned API reference retrieved 2026-10-10; applied to stipulated 3.51.3
primary_evidence.retrieval_operation: Independent direct web open plus follow-up displaying full API body
primary_evidence.evidence_summary: PASSIVE may be incomplete and does not wait for readers/writers; TRUNCATE truncates immediately before successful return. Counters are frames, can be -1 and are undefined for NULL/empty zDb. A competing checkpoint can return SQLITE_BUSY.
primary_evidence.applicability: Applicable WAL database checkpoint operations; frame observations require API argument/return qualifications; truncation is not a future guarantee against later writes.

primary_evidence.title: SQLite URI filenames
primary_evidence.version: Live unversioned official URI reference retrieved 2026-10-10
primary_evidence.retrieval_operation: Independent direct web open plus surrounding-section follow-up
locators: 2 Backwards Compatibility: URI recognition and SQLITE_OPEN_URI
primary_evidence.evidence_summary: Immutable asserts the file cannot change, forces read-only access and skips locking/change detection. False assertions can cause incorrect results or SQLITE_CORRUPT. URI recognition is configurable.
primary_evidence.applicability: Connection actually recognizing immutable URI parameter; real snapshot immutability remains unknown.

limitation_sources.candidate_locator: verification.md claim 5 and Acceptance check 1; source-map.json S2 and AC1
limitation_sources.observation: The candidate mentions pnLog/pnCkpt monitoring without specifying the database-name argument or exceptional counter interpretation. This is a useful prospective observation, rather than a fully specified executable oracle.
limitation_sources.source_conditions: NULL/empty zDb makes both counters undefined; -1 can mean error or non-WAL operation. Frame counts alone do not establish physical zero-byte WAL.
limitation_sources.materiality: Minor: WAL is stipulated, AC1 first verifies WAL activation and also records return code and physical WAL size. Neither a concrete all-database call nor an executed result is asserted; all six substantive dispositions remain supported.

acceptance_check_sources.scope: Target binary/version/VFS WAL activation, local two-process writer/long-reader observations, checkpoint progress and physical file size, actual snapshot opening, NFS support boundary
acceptance_check_sources.concreteness: Concrete observables and reader-release transition are specified; L1 is a minor unresolved counter detail.
acceptance_check_sources.oracle_applicability: Same-host documented WAL behavior and conditional snapshot opening. NFS rejection is a documentation/design boundary, not an executed NFS experiment.

acceptance_check_sources.scope: Repeated matched rollback/WAL p95 measurement on representative catalog workload
acceptance_check_sources.concreteness: Matched data, hardware, durability, concurrency and cache controls plus <=0.60 ratio are specified.
acceptance_check_sources.oracle_applicability: 40 percent conclusion would apply to the representative measured configuration; no measurements are supplied.

independence: Primary evidence was independently retrieved; candidate agreement, citations, counts and hashes were not treated as proof.
